text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000328 bills 99215 at roughly five times the complexity-adjusted expectation, with half of those claims on patients with few or no chronic conditions, but documentation is too thin to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern leans toward concern. The 99215 share runs well above the all-provider rate in every complexity band, including patients with zero conditions. Half of the 99215 claims fall on low-complexity patients, and the sampled examples show visits for diagnoses like Z09 follow-ups, R21 rash and J06.9 upper respiratory infection (e.g., C0196955, C0197943, C0198770), which would rarely need high-complexity decision-making. On the other side, the sampled high-complexity 99215 claims (e.g., C0196824, C0198894) look plausible, and the few charts returned show no documentation shortfalls. Both documented 99215 claims (C0199013, C0199154) supported a high level, but two charts cannot carry a judgment, and the small share of data-reviewed notes with no lab line on the claim is only weak evidence of inflated notes. A reviewer should first request charts specifically for low-complexity 99215 claims such as those listed above, to test whether high MDM is actually documented and whether notes appear templated or cloned."}
